title: Air-gapped artifact mirroring & offline bundle playbook
body:
Purpose and scope:
This playbook captures the end-to-end pattern we use to prepare, transfer, validate, and upgrade Redwood Inference Private deployments in air-gapped (no outbound internet) environments. Focus areas: artifact mirroring, offline registries and bundling, Terraform module knobs for airgap installs, and safe offline upgrade flows.

High-level constraints we assume:
- Customer cluster(s) have zero or tightly-controlled egress (common in regulated/on-prem setups).
- We deliver an artifact bundle that contains container images, Helm charts, operator binaries, and package manager caches as needed.
- All artifacts must be integrity-verified and signed where possible.
- Upgrades should be delta-friendly to keep bundle sizes practical.

Core artifacts we produce:
- OCI image bundle (OCI layout tarball) created by skopeo/crane: images.tar
- Helm chart archive(s) + index.yaml (charts.tgz + index)
- Terraform module state snapshot + plan (tfplan.patched) for offline apply guidance
- Package manager caches: apt/apt-mirror snapshot or yum repos (optional)
- K8s manifests for bootstrap (bootstrap.yaml) and smoke tests
- Signature files (cosign.sig / cosign.pub) and SHA256 checksums file

Recommended on-prem registry pattern:
- Deploy a minimal registry (Harbor/Quay/registry:2) inside the air-gapped network with HTTPs and client cert auth.
- Mirror artifacts into that registry on an upstream sync host (an isolated staging VM inside customer DMZ or supplier-run staging box).
- Keep a small ephemeral registry for rolling upgrades to test pull-through behavior.

Mirroring workflow (detailed):
1) Build source list: gather exact image list from release manifest and customers' pinned versions (images.txt). Keep short, explicit list.
2) Resolve digests: use `crane digest` or `skopeo inspect` to pin image@sha256:... — never rely on tags alone.
3) Sync images to OCI layout: `skopeo sync --src docker --dest oci --dest-tls-verify=false --dest-creds $USER:$PASS --all` to a local staging path.
4) Create OCI tarball: `tar -C /staging -cvf redwood-oci-2026-03-05.tar .` and compute checksums: `sha256sum > checksums.sha256`.
5) Sign artifacts: `cosign sign-blob --key k8s-cosign.key redwood-oci-2026-03-05.tar` and publish matching signature files.
6) Transfer via approved channel (rsync over dedicated line, physically via encrypted drive, or secure courier). Use GPG-encrypted archive in addition to signatures when policy requires.

Offline registry load (customer side):
- Option A: Load OCI tarball into registry via `ctr-remote` or `oras` and push to Harbor. Example: `oras push --manifest-config config.json --media-type=application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json registry.local:443/myproject/image:sha256@...`
- Option B: Use `skopeo copy` from local fs to registry with `skopeo copy oci:/bundle dir docker://registry.local/myproject`
- Ensure registry TLS cert and CA bundle are installed on each node and in containerd/docker config.

Terraform module notes (airgap-focused knobs):
- module "airgap_registry":
  - variables expected (string values):
    - mirror_registry_host (required)
    - mirror_registry_port (default 443)
    - mirror_ca_pem_path (path to CA file on operator machine)
    - auth_username / auth_password (optional, encourage short-lived creds)
    - bundle_archive_path (local path to extracted bundle)
    - terraform_remote_state_bucket (for on-prem state, s3-compatible)
  - outputs (string values):
    - registry_endpoint
    - registry_ca_configmap_name
- Implementation notes for module maintainers:
  - Avoid any provider blocks that require outbound network during plan; plan must be runnable with mocked endpoints if necessary.
  - Use local-exec hooks sparingly and always idempotent. When running destructive operations, require `manual_approval = true` flag.
  - Store large artifact checksums in Terraform state only as metadata; do not store binary blobs.

Example terraform snippet (document only, keep secrets out of repo):
```
module "mirror" {
  source = "github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules//airgap-registry"
  mirror_registry_host = var.mirror_host
  mirror_ca_pem_path = var.mirror_ca
  bundle_archive_path = "/opt/bundles/redwood-oci-2026-03-05.tar"
  manual_approval = true
}
```

Bootstrap and install sequence (operational runbook):
- Pre-check checklist:
  - Confirm storage capacity on registry VM (estimate: uncompressed bundle size * 1.2).
  - Verify host time sync (NTP), DNS records for registry, and internal PKI availability.
  - Operator workstation has CA certs and private cosign keys (offline key handling policy).
- Step 0: Upload and verify bundle checksum and cosign signature.
  - `sha256sum -c checksums.sha256`
  - `cosign verify-blob --key cosign.pub redwood-oci-2026-03-05.tar.cosign`
- Step 1: Extract and load images into registry.
- Step 2: Seed Helm chart repo (charts.tgz -> chartmuseum or simple http server) and update index.yaml.
- Step 3: Apply Terraform modules to provision registry, RBACs, and storage.
- Step 4: Configure cluster containerd with registry mirror. Example (containerd config snippet):
  - `systemd` service restart required after updating `/etc/containerd/config.toml` with `registry.mirrors` entry.
- Step 5: Deploy platform components with `helm install --dependency-update --atomic --wait` referencing the local chart repo.
- Step 6: Run smoke tests (see tests/smoke-suite.md included in bundle).

Upgrade plan (offline-safe):
- Principles:
  - Prepare a delta bundle instead of full rebuild when possible. Only include changed images + new charts.
  - Always pin manifest digests for upgraded images and record previous digests for immediate rollback.
  - Use canary namespaces in customer cluster to validate before global rollout.
- Offline upgrade steps:
  1) Produce upgrade bundle on non-airgapped staging box (list changed images, create oci delta).
  2) Sign and checksum the delta bundle.
  3) Transfer to customer and load to registry.
  4) Run `helm upgrade --install --atomic --wait` to apply new charts referencing pinned digests.
  5) Validate health probes, metrics (CPU, mem), and basic inference smoke tests.
  6) If regression, `helm rollback RELEASE N` using recorded previous revision number and previous manifest files.

Validation and observability (pre/post):
- Pre-install: ensure `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent` is set for all releases in airgapped mode to avoid accidental pulls.
- Post-install: run `kubectl get pods -n redwood -o wide` and check images, node distribution, and pull errors.
- Automated checks (bundle must include):
  - checksums.sha256
  - signature files and verification instructions
  - smoke tests with expected latency thresholds (local inference cold-start).

Security considerations:
- Use Sigstore/cosign to sign images and charts where possible. Keep private signing keys offline and rotate after major releases.
- Enforce registry TLS and mutual TLS for operator machines when policy mandates.
- Store PII-free debug logs in bundle only; sensitive logs must be redacted prior to transfer.

Operational pitfalls and mitigations:
- Large bundles exceed courier limits: create chunked archives and provide reassembly script (sha256 ordered list).
- Registry storage full after incremental upgrades: run `crane digest` + garbage collection plan; document GC windows.
- Terraform drift after manual registry changes: require `manual_approval` and provide `terraform import` snippets to reconcile.

Quick checklist (operator):
- [ ] Confirm artifact list and pin digests
- [ ] Produce OCI layout tar and charts bundle
- [ ] Generate checksums and cosign signatures
- [ ] Transfer bundle to customer (record chain of custody)
- [ ] Run sha256 + cosign verifications on customer side
- [ ] Load images and charts into local registry and chart repo
- [ ] Update container runtime registry config and restart nodes
- [ ] Apply Terraform modules and Helm charts with `--atomic --wait`
- [ ] Run smoke tests and capture logs
- [ ] If any issue, rollback with pinned manifests and helm rollback

Open TODOs and engineering notes (short):
- Add a `tf module` test harness that can run plan/apply against a local mock registry to validate airgap variables without live network.
- Create a small helper utility `rw-airgap-prepare` to produce both full and delta bundles and auto-generate index/checksum/signature artifacts.
- Add support for notary v2 / TUF-based metadata for stronger supply chain guarantees.
- Document recommended retention policy for mirrored images in customer registries (e.g., keep last 3 releases by default).

References and example commands (for operator copy-paste):
- skopeo sync example: `skopeo sync --dest-oci /tmp/redwood-oci --src docker --all docker://ghcr.io/redwood/release:2026-03-05`
- tar and sign: `tar -C /tmp/redwood-oci -cvf redwood-oci-2026-03-05.tar . && sha256sum redwood-oci-2026-03-05.tar > checksums.sha256 && cosign sign-blob --key cosign.key redwood-oci-2026-03-05.tar`
- load to registry: `skopeo copy oci:/tmp/redwood-oci docker://registry.local:443/redwood --dest-creds user:pass`

Contact and escalation:
- Primary owner: Aisha Patel (eng-private-deployments)
- On-call SRE: Marcus Liu
- For Terraform module questions: engineering infra owners via #eng-terraform channel

Document history:
- Draft created 2025-11-10 by Aisha Patel
- Major content rework and Terraform notes added 2026-03-05

This document is intentionally pragmatic and procedural — keep it lightweight and update per-customer details in customer-specific annexes next to this playbook.
